problem: Instance Image Goal Navigation (IIN) methods either fail when the goal image is taken from an arbitrary viewpoint (DRL/IL/foundation-model encoders), or need a dense pre-built 3DGS map of the environment (GaussNav etc.), so they cannot be used in unknown environments with sparse reconstructions.
motivation: Robots searching for a specific object or person from one reference image must recognise instances across viewpoint changes, e.g. a BEV goal image versus the robot's frontal view. Sparse online 3DGS renders of candidate objects contain holes that break feature matching. The paper's observation is that diffusion inpainting can complete these renders, and that semantic and visual context can guide frontier exploration.
key_idea: Build a sparse online 3DGS map, render multi-view images around candidate objects, complete them with a multi-view diffusion inpainter (VCICN) for LoFTR matching against the goal image, and combine semantic and visual context scores to pick frontiers.
insight: Ablations show both viewpoint rendering and inpainting matter: removing NVSM drops HM3D-val-hard SR from 0.63 to 0.43, and removing VCICN drops it to 0.58 (SPL 0.2675 to 0.2204), because sparse renders have large missing regions. Frontier scoring mainly improves efficiency: removing the semantic context score (SCS) or visual context score (VCS) mainly lowers SPL. Too few views (N_R=4) or a bad sampling radius (r_v=0.5 or 2.0) hurt sharply. N_R=12 gives no gain, apparently because of VCICN memory limits.
method: Map Generation Module (MGM): builds an incremental sparse-view 3DGS map (ActiveSplat-style, photometric + depth losses) from RGB-D, plus an occupancy map, frontiers, and a value map of BLIP-2 image-encoder cosine similarity between the current view and the goal image.

Semantic Object Identification Module (SOIM): YOLOv7 boxes + MobileSAM masks find goal-class objects. Mask pixels are mapped to Gaussians to estimate 3D centroids, kept in an object database, and passed on every f_O new viewpoints.

Novel Viewpoint Synthesis Module (NVSM): renders N_R=8 views on an upper hemisphere of radius r_v around the centroid, oriented toward it, and discards views with no feature correspondence to the previous view (occlusion check).

View-Consistent Image Completion Network (VCICN): a multi-view latent diffusion inpainter initialised from MVInpainter-O. The robot view is the unmasked reference and the other views are masked. It is conditioned on a CLIP text prompt of the goal class and fine-tuned with an MSE noise loss.
Feature Extraction Module (FEM): Efficient LoFTR counts correspondences between the goal image and each completed view. The max score s_max is compared with a threshold τ_m to declare a match.

Exploration Planner (EP): picks the frontier maximising α·inverse distance + β·visual object score E_t(f) + δ·average semantic value. On a match it plans with FMM to the instance centroid, stopping within 1 m.

setting.backbone: Modular: YOLOv7 + MobileSAM, BLIP-2 image encoder (frozen), ActiveSplat-style 3DGS, MVInpainter-O diffusion (fine-tuned as VCICN), Efficient LoFTR, FMM planner
setting.training_data: Only VCICN is fine-tuned, on about 19,200 images: ~2,000 objects x 8 views (16,000) collected from 145 HM3DSem-v0.2 training scenes over 6 classes, plus 400 people x 8 views from EgoBody. It is initialised from MVInpainter-O and trained for 10k steps in 46 h on an RTX 4090.
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB-D + pose, plus a single goal image
setting.action_space: Frontier selection with FMM path following on the occupancy map
setting.privileged: none (pose is assumed given in simulation; real-world pose from LF-SLAM)

numbers.eval_set_note: 100 episodes from the HM3DSem-v0.2 validation set (HM3D-val)
numbers.backbone: YOLOv7 + MobileSAM + BLIP-2 encoder + fine-tuned MVInpainter (VCICN) + Efficient LoFTR
numbers.extra: VCICN fine-tuned on simulated + EgoBody data; success radius 1 m

numbers_note: Simulation used only 100 episodes per validation set. Ablation numbers are in Table III; the real-world w/o VCICN variant scored SR 0.60, SPL 0.36.
results: SplatSearch reaches SR 0.70 / SPL 0.3740 on HM3D-val and SR 0.63 / SPL 0.2675 on HM3D-val-hard, beating the strongest baseline UniGoal (0.69/0.2837 and 0.59/0.1738). It is comparable in the real world (SR 0.76, SPL 0.48).
limitations: YOLOv7 restricts detection to a fixed set of object categories.
The multi-module pipeline is fragile to failures of individual modules. The diffusion step takes about 7 s per call and has memory limits, so N_R=12 did not help.
Evaluation is small (100 episodes, 25 real trials) and assumes a static environment.
